correctness.rationale: The exact event is proved through possible unit-ball centers and two spherical caps. Uniform local normal-coordinate rescaling yields a spherical Euclidean-ball factor and an explicit double radial moment, valid for every centrally symmetric convex body in all dimensions d>=2. The radial integral is evaluated by a finite binomial sum. Polar volume normalization and strict Jensen prove the ball minimizer; a tangent-line convexity inequality proves the quantitative variance bound; thin rectangular boxes prove absence of an upper bound. The actual standalone standard-library checker reproduces exact d=2,3,4 constants and independent numerical limits without being used in place of proof.

value.rationale: The fixed-two-point Wendel-type ball-spindle absorption probability is a recognized geometric-probability object, whose vanishing small-radius limit was known for uniform balls. The new asymptotic measures the exact rare antipodal direction event in every centrally symmetric convex body, exposes a nonstandard (3d-1)-st radial moment and yields sharp fixed-volume Euclidean-ball rigidity and quantitative stability. Unboundedness for thin bodies completes the meaningful extremal picture. The claim neither relies on a gimmick parameter nor on numerical enumeration.
